variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are assigned using a colon (:).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
int: 42
float: 3.14
char: "a"
str: "hello"
bool: 1b
sym: `hello
data_types.notes: K supports standard primitives plus symbols (`) which are interned strings used for fast equality checks.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
sum: 3 + 4
diff: 10 - 5
prod: 2 * 3
quot: 10 % 2

eq: 1 = 1
neq: 1 ~ 2
gt: 2 > 1
operators.notes: Operators evaluate strictly right-to-left. No operator precedence. Division is %.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: The cond operator ($) takes a condition, true branch, and false branch. It can be extended: $[cond1; res1; cond2; res2; default].

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
/ Array-oriented approach
squares: {x*x} 0 1 2 3 4

/ Explicit loop
x: 0
do[5; x:x+1]
for_loop.notes: do[n; ...] executes the block n times. Most looping is avoided in favor of vector operations.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: while[cond; block] executes until cond evaluates to 0 or false.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions are enclosed in {}. Arguments are specified in brackets, or implicitly use x, y, and z.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Lists (arrays) are created by separating items with spaces or semicolons in parentheses. # gets the length or shape.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Dictionaries (maps) are created using the bang operator (!) joining a list of keys and a list of values.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Trap (@) catches errors. It takes a function, its arguments, and a callback function for the error case.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in K
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: K uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: K is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: K provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: K converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: K treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: K formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: K executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: K indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: K emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in K
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: K uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: K stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: K uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: K provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: K loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
